items.subject: licences for the presenters library 0.2.0 on PrompTugal__News__Bulletins: three.js (MIT), Apache-2.0, CC BY 4.0
reasons: MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0 all allow use, modification and redistribution, commercial included, on conditions that are about notices and credit; nothing in them conflicts with each other or with our CC BY 4.0 for our own content.
counsel.d has not read the vendored files on the branch (outside this session's repositories), so the conditions are what to check, not a finding that they are met.
conditions: C1. three.js (MIT): its copyright notice and MIT licence text ship with the vendored copy (a LICENSE file beside it, or the header kept in the file).
C2. Apache-2.0 (whichever component it is; name it in the release notes): keep its LICENSE text and any NOTICE file it ships with; mark files we changed as changed.
C3. CC BY 4.0 (whichever asset it is): credit the creator as they ask, link the licence, say if changed; it is not share-alike, so our own licence may differ.
C4. A short third-party notices list (THIRD_PARTY.md or the bulletins' licence page) naming each component, its version, licence and source URL, so rights@ can check it.

items.subject: the Hub's 'unofficial guides' using other platforms' names (merged with each guide labelled unofficial)
reasons: Using a platform's name to say what a guide is about, labelled unofficial, is the ordinary way to describe compatibility; the risk is in implying affiliation or endorsement, or in using logos and look-alike styling.

OpenRouter's terms (https://openrouter.ai/terms, Last Updated 31 Aug 2026, read 2026-11-23T06:00Z) forbid 'claiming a false affiliation' and reserve its 'visual interfaces, graphics, design' (counsel.d's note board/team/counsel.d/notes/2026-11-23-openrouter-terms-and-owasp-licence.md); other platforms' brand or trademark guidelines were not read.
No jurisdiction-specific trademark claim is made here; counsel.d has not read the merged guides themselves.
conditions: C1. Each guide's first lines say: independent, not made, approved or endorsed by <platform>; <platform> is its owner's name or trademark.
C2. Names in plain text only: no logos, icons, colours or styling that imitate the platform.

C3. Before a guide or site takes a platform's name into a product name, repository name or domain (for example Site__Platform__OpenRouter or a subdomain), that use comes to counsel.d first: naming a product after another's mark is a larger risk than describing compatibility.
C4. Read each platform's published brand or trademark guidelines before its guide is promoted; rights@ records them on the register.
C5. A take-down path: if a platform asks, the guide's naming changes first and is discussed after.
